## Research Overview

Aleka Melese Ayalew was involved in a 2024 study on early-stage cardiomegaly detection and classification from X-ray images, serving as the lead author responsible for conceptualization, methodology, software, and writing the original draft.

## Study Methodology

The research developed a model using CNN, Inception, DenseNet-169, and ResNet-50 for better identification of cardiomegaly disease. The study utilized advanced image enhancement techniques, including CLAHE and BM3D noise filtering, which significantly improved the quality of the X-ray images and, consequently, the accuracy of the model.

## Key Results

The ResNet-50 model achieved reliable and accurate training, validation, and testing accuracy of 100%, 100%, and 99.8%, respectively. The models can accurately detect early signs of cardiomegaly, supported by visualization techniques like Grad-CAM, which underscores its potential for facilitating earlier interventions and improved patient outcomes in clinical practice.

The research was published in October 2024 in the journal "Intelligent Systems with Applications."

The study proposes a real-time malaria monitoring and detection system using an Internet of Things (IoT) framework that collects real-time symptom data via wearable sensors, employs edge computing for processing, utilizes cloud infrastructure for data storage, and applies machine learning models for data analysis.

### System Components

The five key components of the framework are wearable sensor-based symptom data collection and uploading, edge (fog) computing, cloud infrastructure, machine learning models for data analysis, and doctors (physicians).

The study compares four machine learning techniques: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), and Naïve Bayes, with SVM outperforming the other algorithms, achieving 98% training accuracy, 96% test accuracy, and a 95% AUC score.
